PullRequest.Title: mcp: make assisted setup destination-aware
PullRequest.Body:
## Summary

- Choose the destination before package-assisted MCP setup, including Copilot Global.
- Preserve the server's stdio, HTTP, or SSE configuration and use package manifests when available.
- Keep collected values out of generated files and require explicit approval before falling back to VS Code configuration.

Stacked on #337838. The base is `agents/p3-copilot-global-manual`; main integration is intentionally deferred.

<details>
<summary>Technical context for AI-assisted review</summary>

### Intent and previous behavior

Package setup previously generated a stdio-shaped configuration before choosing its destination. That prevented the prompt and input handling from matching the destination, excluded Copilot Global, and overwrote remote transport intent.

### Implementation

Core selects the destination using the existing install-target service, global picker, and workspace-file defaults. It supplies a destination schema to the extension. The extension validates and extracts exactly one named server without partially converting its dialect; core then normalizes through the shared converters, and the existing scanner owns the final file representation and safe write.

Usable package manifests still bypass the model. Their inputs and unsupported fields remain intact so core can offer a safe destination instead of stripping metadata. Workspace-root generation can retain required VS Code fields or SSE intent, but those configurations require explicit approval to use the legacy workspace file.

### Behavior and constraints

- Manual setup retains its question order and the existing global labels and path descriptions.
- VS Code input answers become opaque references before reaching the model, including when embedded inside URLs, arguments, or headers. Values go through the existing saved-input path rather than the configuration file.
- Copilot Global prompts request uppercase environment-variable names, not values. Generated references are retained, and the completion notification explains that variables must be set on the agent-host machine before a new session.
- Validation rejects malformed or ambiguous output, missing or altered input references, and mismatched command output formats without logging sensitive payloads. Older callers without a destination format retain the VS Code default; incompatible extension output produces an explicit error.
- Explicit file targets are never silently redirected. Cancellation and policy rejection occur without writes, and package configurations requiring unresolved inputs cannot be handed to the current agent session.
- Existing Copilot-home lookup, authority-scoped discovery behavior, shared workspace eligibility, and scanner concurrency protections remain unchanged. No agent-host protocol or general destination framework is added.

</details>

Findings.ConfidenceRationale: The changed call order, prior package guard, IPC implementation, lack of caching, and five-second bound are all explicit in code and tests. Exact typical IPC duration is environment-dependent, which affects severity but not the mechanism or critical-path reachability.
Findings.PerformanceResource: A main-process or remote-agent IPC call that resolves the shell environment and Copilot home directory
Findings.PerformanceScaling: The uncached lookup runs once, serially, on every package-assisted setup that selects the Global scope, including setups that subsequently choose the VS Code user configuration; each invocation can wait for the full five-second timeout.
Findings.PerformanceOutcome: The add-server workflow is blocked before the global destination picker appears, adding avoidable latency of up to five seconds.
Findings.PreviousBehavior: Package-assisted NPM, Pip, NuGet, and Docker additions generated the configuration first and then selected the install target; the old Copilot-global resource lookup was guarded to manual stdio/HTTP server types, so a package addition targeting VS Code user configuration made no discovery IPC call.
Findings.ChangedBehavior: Package-assisted additions now call getSetupDestination before asking for package details, and selecting Global immediately awaits getConfigurationResource before presenting the Copilot Global versus VS Code picker.
Findings.CausalDiffEvidence: Added line 371 awaits `_copilotGlobalConfigurationService.getConfigurationResource()` in the new pre-generation destination path. The added package branch at lines 556-568 calls that path before `getAssistedConfig`; the service performs `ProxyChannel...load()` against the main process or remote agent and wraps it in a 5000 ms timeout.
Findings.Title: Do not block the destination picker on Copilot-home discovery
Findings.Impact: With Agent Host enabled, choosing Global for any package-assisted MCP install can leave the UI waiting before the next picker is shown; slow remote IPC or shell-environment startup can impose the entire five-second timeout even when the user only wants the VS Code user configuration.
Findings.Evidence: `McpCopilotGlobalConfigurationService.getConfigurationResource` awaits `loadDiscoveryData`; desktop and remote implementations cross IPC, and `NativeMcpDiscoveryHelperService.load` may await shell-environment resolution. Its test explicitly establishes a five-second timeout. The new entry-point test for choosing `User Configuration (deprecated)` changes the expected discovery lookups from 0 to 1, directly confirming that the diff adds this boundary even when Copilot Global is not selected.
Findings.Recommendation: Present the global destination choices without awaiting discovery and resolve the Copilot resource only if Copilot Global is selected, or consume a cached/coalesced discovery result already populated by native MCP discovery. Preserve the current destination-first ordering for generation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Package-assisted MCP setup targeting Global, then choosing legacy VS Code user configuration
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Server-type picker -> install-target picker -> newly awaited Copilot-home discovery -> global-destination picker -> package-name input -> registry validation -> consent -> optional manifest retrieval or model generation -> server-name input -> install/write. The discovery IPC must finish before the destination picker and all subsequent work.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Load native discovery data, including shell environment and Copilot home, through the main-process or remote-agent channel
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One uncached IPC per package-assisted invocation after selecting Global
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Package-assisted additions did not enter the old manual stdio/HTTP Copilot-global lookup, so legacy VS Code package installs performed zero such calls.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Blocks presentation of the Copilot Global versus VS Code picker; the service permits a five-second wait

ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One request per package validation attempt; retries are user-driven
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same registry request occurred before the diff.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before consent and generation

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Run the utility language-model tool loop when no usable manifest is available
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One or more model requests for one package, bounded by the existing conversation/tool limits
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Same assisted model loop occurred before the diff; the destination-specific prompt/schema changes payload content, not request multiplicity.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Must finish before configuration naming and installation

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Install the server into the VS Code MCP configuration and save up to five collected input values
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One configuration install plus at most five sequential saved-input operations
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same final install and saved-input path existed before the diff.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One setup request and one package; the new discovery boundary has effective cardinality one per invocation, with no cache or coalescing across invocations.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The destination lookup is serialized ahead of the picker and package work. Registry validation, generation, install, and saved-input writes remain ordered; no aggregate concurrency burst is introduced.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Copilot-home discovery is uncached and repeated for each setup. Package registry/model behavior is unchanged; a usable package manifest bypasses model generation.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High: changed control flow, prior behavior, IPC implementation, timeout, and test lookup counts all directly establish the mechanism.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Typical IPC and shell-environment latency varies, and this is an infrequent setup workflow, but tests establish a possible five-second wait and the newly serialized boundary is certain.
Scenarios.Verdict: Reportable medium-severity latency regression because an unnecessary uncached IPC is added to the critical path even when the user ultimately selects VS Code configuration.

Scenarios.Scenario: Package-assisted MCP setup targeting Copilot Global
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Destination selection and Copilot-home discovery must complete before package input, registry validation, consent, manifest/model generation, name input, policy check, one configuration-file write, and editor open.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve the agent-host Copilot configuration resource
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Package-assisted setup could not target Copilot Global, so this boundary was absent for packages.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required to obtain the selected Copilot Global resource, but currently blocks before the user chooses that destination

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Validate package metadata and, absent a usable manifest, call the language model
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One registry request plus bounded model turns for one package
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Package validation and generation already used these boundaries.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required before a generated server can be written

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Read/edit/write the Copilot Global MCP configuration through the resource scanner
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One serialized file update for one server
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: Package-assisted configurations were installed only through VS Code configuration paths.

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One package and one generated server per invocation; generated tool questions are bounded at five.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The destination IPC, validation, generation, and write are sequential on the user-visible path. Existing setup work is held behind consent where required; scanner writes are serialized by resource.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Discovery is uncached; registry responses are not cached here. A package manifest is a positive fast path that avoids all model calls. There is no negative-cache behavior changed by this diff.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High for the boundary and serialization; no collection fan-out or unbounded allocation is present.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: The added Copilot Global capability necessarily needs a resource and write; only the preselection scheduling creates avoidable latency. File size and normal IPC duration are unknown but cardinality is one.
Scenarios.Verdict: No additional finding beyond the shared eager-discovery issue; registry/model/write work is bounded and required by the new destination.

Scenarios.Scenario: Package-assisted MCP setup targeting a workspace root or legacy workspace file
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Install-target picker -> workspace configuration existence check/picker -> package input -> registry validation -> consent -> manifest/model generation -> compatibility recheck -> name input -> install/write -> saved inputs.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve whether .vscode/mcp.json exists to choose the workspace dialect
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One file-service resolve per package setup when root configuration is enabled
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The same resolve occurred after generation during final target selection; the diff moves it earlier without increasing cardinality.
ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Now occurs before generation because the schema depends on the destination

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Package registry validation and optional utility-model generation
ExpensiveBoundaries.Cardinality: One registry request and bounded model turns per package attempt

ExpensiveBoundaries.CriticalPathEffect: Required persistence at the end of setup

Scenarios.ScalingInput: One workspace folder, one package, one server; up to five generated input values.
Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: The legacy-file resolve is awaited before package work; subsequent registry/model/write operations are serial. Saved-input writes are sequential and bounded at five, as before.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: The legacy-file existence check is not cached within the helper, but it occurs once before generation. Manifest success bypasses model generation; retries reuse the already selected format.
Scenarios.MechanismConfidence: High that boundary count remains one and no fan-out is introduced.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: Workspace file-system latency varies, especially remotely, but the diff does not add another resolve and the earlier placement is required to choose the generation schema.
Scenarios.Verdict: No reportable regression: the file check is moved, not multiplied, and the destination must be known before destination-specific generation.

Scenarios.Scenario: Manual stdio or HTTP server addition
Scenarios.CriticalPath: Server details input -> server-name input -> install-target/destination selection -> optional Copilot-home discovery -> policy check -> one configuration write and editor open.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Resolve Copilot Global configuration resource when Global is selected
ExpensiveBoundaries.PreviousBehavior: The removed manual branch performed the same lookup at the same post-details stage.

ExpensiveBoundaries.Operation: Write one server to the selected MCP configuration

Scenarios.EffectiveConcurrency: All user prompts and persistence steps are sequential; scanner writes are serialized per resource.
Scenarios.CacheBehavior: Copilot-home lookup remains uncached, but this scenario already performed it before the diff. No changed cache keys or negative-cache states.
Scenarios.MagnitudeUncertainty: No material uncertainty affects the before/after comparison; this path is behaviorally reorganized but does not add expensive work.
Scenarios.Verdict: No performance finding because expensive-boundary cardinality and placement for manual additions are effectively unchanged.

Analysis.Summary: Reviewed all 12 changed files and traced package-assisted and manual MCP addition paths through destination selection, registry/model calls, IPC discovery, filesystem persistence, input storage, cancellation, and scanner serialization. Submitted one medium-severity eager-work finding for the newly serialized, uncached Copilot-home IPC on package installs that may still choose VS Code configuration. No other changed path introduced realistic fan-out, unbounded retention, concurrency bursts, or hot-loop work.

Stats.CostNote: Copilot SDK reports nano-AI units and model billing multipliers; it does not provide a USD conversion.
